units: metres, and km/h for speed limits
axes: right-handed, +X left, +Y up, +Z forward — AC's own, the same as glTF
height_note: Lane points are authored at road level — sampled against Fukuoka's collision mesh the median sits 0.001 m above it. This is the opposite of an AC AI line, which floats at the recording car's ride height. Use the y as given.
interpolation_note: Points are sparse control points, not a sampled line: 2 points can span 110 m. The file does not say how CSP interpolates between them, so lengths here are chord lengths.

junctions.note: Derived from geometry, not read from the file — CSP stores no lane graph. A merge is a lane ending on top of another; a branch is one starting on top of another. distance_m is the evidence for each.

dead_ends.note: Lanes whose last point joins nothing within the tolerance. Traffic reaching one has nowhere to go and has to be despawned or turned round.
